battle.name: 汪達爾戰爭
battle.theater: 北非迦太基與突尼斯灣
battle.brief: 公元533年，查士丁尼一世命貝利撒留率一萬步兵、五千騎兵征北非：六月出航，九月登陸突尼斯灣，十日北進至迦太基以南十里的阿德底斯姆，擊潰蓋利默的汪達爾騎兵；十二月再於特里卡馬魯姆破之，汪達爾王次年三月投降。卡面短劍非此戰主兵器，卻是帝國盾步兵的配備短兵：盾在前，劍在腰，只求刺突。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries:
汪達爾戰爭是東羅馬帝國與汪達爾-阿蘭王國在北非的一場戰爭，時間在公元533至534年，戰場在今日突尼西亞與阿爾及利亞東部。東羅馬一方由皇帝查士丁尼一世直接統率，遠征軍由大將貝利撒留率領：步兵一萬人，部分出自野戰軍，部分是蠻盟軍；騎兵五千人；另有貝利撒留自帶的布契拉里近衛騎兵一千五百至二千人，以及兩支以騎射為主的盟軍——六百名匈人與四百名赫魯利人。艦隊方面，五百艘運輸船載著約三萬名水手，由海軍上將卡洛尼馬斯指揮，另有九十二艘德羅蒙戰船護衛。指揮體系很簡單：貝利撒留在前線獨斷，後方由太監所羅門以參謀長身分統籌軍務，前禁衛軍長官阿爾克勞斯管後勤，色雷斯人魯菲努斯與匈人艾甘分領騎兵，亞美尼亞人約翰帶三百騎兵充當先鋒，蠻盟軍軍官西里爾率四百人隨艦前往撒丁島。君士坦丁堡內部並非一致支持：財政官員不願再掏錢，軍方厭惡波斯戰事，國庫仍然吃緊，唯一公開反對遠征的是大權在握的卡帕多西亞人約翰，但皇帝沒有採納他的意見。
汪達爾一方則由國王蓋利默全權指揮。這個王國不是常備軍國家，而是以全族成年男子徵集的部落式軍隊：估計兵力二萬至四萬人，其中絕大多數是騎兵，而且精銳與戰船都遠在撒丁島。國王的兄弟阿馬圖斯坐鎮迦太基，兄弟察佐帶五千人與一百二十艘精銳戰艦遠征撒丁島平叛，姪子吉巴蒙德領兩千人。祕書博尼法提烏斯奉命把王室財寶裝船，準備一旦失守就送往西班牙的西哥德王國。汪達爾的處境同時被三件事削弱：北非的羅馬-阿非利加居民敵意甚深，王國內仍有擁護前王希爾德里克的派系，南方沙漠的柏柏爾部落態度游移，誰贏就向誰效忠。戰前雙方都在外交上拉攏盟友：蓋利默派使團赴西哥德王國求援，狄奧迪斯盛情接待卻在得知迦太基失守後當場拒絕；查士丁尼則確保了東哥德王國的中立，並取得西西里島敘拉古港作為艦隊的補給基地。
countriesEn: The Vandalic War was a war fought in North Africa between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Vandal-Arabic kingdom in the years 533 and 534, on ground that is now Tunisia and eastern Algeria. On the Roman side the command lay with the emperor Justinian I himself, and the expeditionary force was led by the general Belisarius: ten thousand foot, drawn partly from the field army and partly from the foederati; five thousand horse; together with the bucephalarian guard of one thousand five hundred to two thousand men that Belisarius brought with him, and two auxiliary bodies whose strength lay in shooting from horseback, six hundred Huns and four hundred Heruli. On the naval side, five hundred transports carrying about thirty thousand sailors were under the admiral Calonymus, with ninety-two dromons in escort. The command structure was simple: Belisarius decided on the spot in the front line, while at the rear the eunuch Solomon acted as domesticus and ran the military staff, the former captain of the guard Alcazar looked after logistics, the Thracian Rufinus and the Hun Aigan led the cavalry between them, the Armenian John took three hundred cavalry as a vanguard, and the foederatus officer Cyril went with the fleet to Sardinia with four hundred men. Opinion in Constantinople was not united: the finance officials were unwilling to pay for another war, the army was worn out by the Persian war, and the treasury was still strained. The only man of high standing to oppose the expedition openly was John the Cappadocian, and the emperor ignored him. The Vandal side was entirely under the command of the king, Gelimer. This was not a state with a standing army but one that levied the whole tribe's able-bodied men: the force is estimated at twenty to forty thousand, the great majority of it cavalry, with the best troops and the warships far away in Sardinia. The king's brother Ammatas held Carthage, his brother Tzazo had taken five thousand men and one hundred and twenty war galleys to Sardinia to put down a revolt, and his nephew Gibamund led two thousand. The secretary Bonifatius was ordered to load the royal treasure onto ships so that it could be sent to the Visigothic kingdom in Spain if the position was lost. The Vandal position was weakened at the same time by three things: deep hostility among the Roman-African population of North Africa, a surviving party in the kingdom that backed the former king Hilderic, and the shifting attitude of the Berber tribes of the southern deserts, who would side with whoever won. Both rulers worked the diplomatic channel before the war: Gelimer sent an embassy to the Visigothic court to ask for help, and Theudis received it courteously, then refused it outright once he learned that Carthage had fallen; Justinian in turn secured the neutrality of the Ostrogothic kingdom and obtained the port of Syracuse in Sicily as a supply base for his fleet.
people:
這場戰爭留下名字的人很多，東羅馬一方尤其完整。皇帝查士丁尼一世是整場戰爭的決策者：出兵的藉口、艦隊的規模、將官的挑選都在他手上；君士坦丁堡牧首與狄奧多拉在出航當日出席典禮，說明這次遠征被當作帝國的宗教事業，而不是單純的領土行動。貝利撒留是前線唯一的主帥，選他出來有兩個理由：他通拉丁語，也嚴守軍紀，而北非居民講拉丁語、並且吃夠了汪達爾人的苦，所以「以解放者姿態出現」是他能贏得當地支持的原因。他的妻子安東尼娜隨軍，負責後勤與軍需，在阿德底斯姆率步兵趕到戰場的正是她；他的祕書普羅科匹厄斯隨軍記錄，寫成《汪達爾戰爭史》，是這場戰爭最核心的一手史料。參謀長所羅門是太監出身，與海軍上將卡洛尼馬斯一同掌管軍務；亞美尼亞人約翰領三百騎兵作先鋒，在特里卡馬魯姆反覆衝鋒汪達爾軍中央，最後陣亡；匈人艾甘與色雷斯人魯菲努斯分領騎兵；蠻盟軍軍官西里爾後來奉命帶著察佐的首級去撒丁島與科西嘉島，宣示帝國對這些島嶼的主權。
汪達爾一方留下姓名的四人都是國王的血親與近臣。國王蓋利默在530年推翻堂兄希爾德里克、囚禁他，533年又下令處決希爾德里克及其親屬；他在迦太基失守後退往布拉雷吉亞，集結逃兵與柏柏爾盟友，決心奪回都城。他的兄弟阿馬圖斯在阿德底斯姆前哨被羅馬先鋒擊斃；兄弟察佐帶五千人與一百二十艘戰艦在撒丁島平定戈達斯的叛亂，聞訊回援，在特里卡馬魯姆率中央陣地反衝時陣亡；姪子吉巴蒙德領兩千人攻擊羅馬軍左翼，遭匈人側擊全軍覆沒，本人陣亡。祕書博尼法提烏斯奉命把王室財寶運往西哥德，卻因逆風無法啟航，最後把寶藏交給了羅馬人，汪達爾王國的家底因此落入帝國之手。另一個關鍵人物是赫魯利人法拉斯，他率四百人圍困蓋利默於巴巴山上的梅迪烏斯堡壘直到次年三月。稍場外的一個角色是西哥德王狄奧迪斯：他在宴席上聽完汪達爾使團的陳述之後，只讓他們去海邊看看國內的情形。
peopleEn: A good many people are named in this war, and the Roman side is the better documented. The emperor Justinian I was the man who decided everything: the pretext for the war, the size of the fleet, the choice of commanders were all his. The empress Theodora and the patriarch of Constantinople attended the ceremony on the day of departure, which shows that the expedition was treated as a religious undertaking of the empire rather than a mere grab for territory. Belisarius was the single commander in the field, and there were two reasons he was picked: he knew Latin, and he kept strict discipline, and the people of North Africa spoke Latin and had suffered enough under the Vandals, so that appearing as a liberator was the key to winning their support. His wife Antonina marched with him, took charge of supply and logistics, and it was she who led the infantry up to the field at Ad Decimum. His secretary Procopius marched as well and wrote the History of the Wars, the central primary source for the whole campaign. The domesticus Solomon was a eunuch, and together with the admiral Calonymus handled the military staff; the Armenian John led three hundred cavalry as a vanguard, charged repeatedly into the Vandal centre at Tricamarum and was killed there; the Hun Aigan and the Thracian Rufinus commanded the cavalry between them; the foederatus officer Cyril later carried the head of Tzazo to Sardinia and Corsica to proclaim the empire's sovereignty over those islands. Four names survive on the Vandal side, all of them the king's own kin or close associates. Gelimer had overthrown and imprisoned his cousin Hilderic in 530, and in 533 he ordered the execution of Hilderic and his relatives; after the loss of Carthage he withdrew to Bulla Regia, gathered the fugitives and his Berber allies, and resolved to retake his capital. His brother Ammatas was killed by the Roman vanguard in the skirmish before Ad Decimum; his brother Tzazo, who had taken five thousand men and one hundred and twenty warships to Sardinia to put down Godas's revolt, turned back on the news and was killed leading the Vandal centre at Tricamarum; his nephew Gibamund, leading two thousand men against the Roman left, was cut up by the Huns and perished with them. The secretary Bonifatius was charged with carrying the royal treasure to the Visigoths, but the wind was against him and he finally handed the treasure over to the Romans, so that the whole fortune of the Vandal kingdom passed into imperial hands. Another key figure was Pharas the Herulian, who with four hundred men blockaded Gelimer in the fortress of Medeum on the Mountains of the Moon until March of the following year. One figure stood slightly off the field, the Visigothic king Theudis, who at the end of the Vandal embassy's audience only sent the envoys to the seashore to see for themselves how things stood at home.
kits:
先要說清楚卡面上這把兵器的位置：羅馬短劍（gladius）在533年已經不是帝國軍隊的制式主兵器。晚期羅馬的步兵與禁衛軍早已改用更長的長劍（spatha），短劍退居次要角色，多留在海軍陸戰隊、警衛勤務以及一切需要輕便短兵的地方；但它並未從軍械庫裡消失，帝國軍的短兵編制、軍需清冊與徵發制度裡都還看得到它的份額。真正決定阿德底斯姆與特里卡馬魯姆兩戰勝負的，是另外兩種兵器：帝國重裝騎兵手中的長矛（kontos）與長劍，以及汪達爾騎兵手中的長矛與長劍。
把短劍放進這場戰爭的裝備表，理由不在它是否上陣，而在它所代表的那條技術路線：盾在前，劍備於腰，短兵相接靠盾的邊緣與刺突的節奏。晚期羅馬的「盾兵」（scutarii）裝備是橢圓形大盾（scutum）、一至兩支標槍與投槍、一支長矛，配一把短兵；到了東羅馬時代，步兵的編制仍以「持盾列」為骨架，盾牌大而厚，成排前進，長矛平舉，刺不到時就用短劍的刺突解決貼身糾纏。帝國遠征軍這次帶上非洲的正是這種盾步兵與一支精銳的槍騎兵：步兵一萬人裡面有野戰軍與蠻盟軍，配大盾、長矛與短兵；騎兵五千人裡面是裝甲的鎧甲騎兵（kataphraktoi），配長矛、長劍與小圓盾。汪達爾一方在裝備上幾乎是羅馬式的翻版：這支部族本身就是羅馬的盟軍出身，國家機器照抄羅馬制度，迦太基近郊博爾傑杰迪德出土的汪達爾騎兵鑲嵌畫裡，騎士戴頭盔、披鎖子或鱗甲、持圓盾與長矛，身旁是同樣的長劍。畫裡沒有短劍，這說明卡面上的短劍在這場戰爭的騎兵戰裡確實沒有位置。
其他裝備同樣要交代清楚。遠征的載體是船：五百艘運輸船，裝人、裝馬、裝糧、裝攻城器械，另有九十二艘德羅蒙重巡洋艦護衛；德羅蒙是雙列槳的巨型戰艦，撞角加厚，專為撞擊敵艦而造。遠征軍在梅托尼上岸整頓時，隨軍麵包黴爛引發痢疾，一次病倒五百人，說明糧食的保存與淡水補給是這場跨海戰爭最脆弱的一環；艦隊在佩林圖斯等馬五天、在阿比多斯等風四天，也說明遠征不是計畫好就走的遠足。給養方面，貝利撒留的作戰半徑必須靠沿途徵收與嚴禁劫掠來維持，他因部屬偷摘果園水果而當眾懲處，正是為了不讓軍隊把當地居民推向蓋利默一方。攻城與守城方面，迦太基是王國境內唯一沒有拆牆的城市，其城牆、港口與引水渠在534年的一整個冬天裡決定了攻防的節奏；蓋利默切斷城外引水渠，就是用水利工程卡住城內的用水。汪達爾人的船隊是另一個被低估的變數：一百二十艘精銳戰艦加五千人遠在撒丁島，等於替登陸的帝國軍清空了海峽與本土之間的屏障——這是全場戰爭最要命的一個錯誤。
kitsEn: First the place of the weapon on the card has to be made clear: by 533 the Roman gladius was no longer the standard main weapon of the imperial army. Late Roman infantry and the imperial guard had long since taken to the longer spatha, and the short sword had been pushed into a secondary role, surviving mostly in the marines of the fleet, in police and guard duties, and in every place where a light short weapon was wanted. It had not vanished from the arsenals: the short-arms tables, the supply lists and the levy system of the imperial army all still carry a share for it. The weapons that actually decided the two battles of Ad Decimum and Tricamarum were two others: the long lance and the long sword in the hands of the imperial heavy cavalry, and the lance and the long sword of the Vandal horse. The reason for putting the gladius into the equipment table of this war lies not in whether it went into the line, but in the line of technique it stands for: the shield in front, the sword at the waist, and close combat settled by the edge of the shield and by the rhythm of the thrust. The late Roman scutarii carried the large oval scutum, one or two javelins, a spear, and a short sword; and by the Byzantine period the infantry were still organised on the skeleton of the shield line, big thick shields moving up in ranks, spears levelled, and when the spear could not reach, the short sword's thrust settling the entanglement at close quarters. What the expedition carried to Africa was exactly this: shield infantry and a body of lancers, with the ten thousand foot drawn from the field army and the foederati, equipped with large shields, spears and short weapons, and among the five thousand horse the armoured kataphraktoi, with lance, spatha and small round shield. On the Vandal side the equipment is very nearly a Roman copy: the tribe itself came out of the Roman foederati, and the state copied Roman institutions, so that the mosaic of Vandal horsemen found at Bordj Djedid near Carthage shows riders in helmets, in mail or scale, with round shields and lances, and the same long sword at their side. There is no gladius in the picture, which shows that the weapon on the card had no place in the cavalry fighting of this war. The rest of the equipment has to be described as well. The vehicle of the expedition was the ship: five hundred transports carrying men, horses, grain and siege engines, escorted by ninety-two dromons, those heavy cruisers with two banks of oars and reinforced rams built to smash enemy hulls. When the expedition disembarked at Methoni, mouldy bread in the stores brought on dysentery and put five hundred men down at once, which shows how fragile the grain and the fresh water were in a war carried across the sea; the fleet waited five days at Perinthus for horses and four days at Abydos for wind, which shows too that an expedition was not a stroll undertaken once the plan was drawn. On supply, the radius of Belisarius's operations had to be sustained by requisition along the line and by a strict ban on plunder, and his public punishment of soldiers caught stealing fruit from an orchard was intended to keep the army from driving the local population into Gelimer's arms. On attack and defence, Carthage was the one city in the kingdom whose walls had not been pulled down, and its walls, its harbour and its aqueduct set the rhythm of the whole defensive winter of 534; Gelimer's cutting of the aqueduct outside the city was an attempt to strangle the town's water supply by works of hydraulics. The Vandal fleet was the other underestimated variable: one hundred and twenty war galleys and five thousand men away in Sardinia cleared the strait and the barrier between the sea and the homeland for the invading army, and that was the single most damaging error of the whole war.
tactics:
貝利撒留的整套打法可以拆成七步。第一步是渡海與不宣而戰。艦隊於533年6月21日前後在查士丁尼、狄奧多拉與牧首面前出海，經佩林圖斯、阿比多斯、達達尼爾海峽、梅托尼，繞扎金索斯島過愛奧尼亞海，因逆風與淡水變質拖慢行程；抵西西里後，普羅科匹厄斯被派往敘拉古打探，得到關鍵情報：汪達爾人根本不知道帝國艦隊來了，而蓋利默已隨察佐遠征撒丁島。貝利撒留立刻重新登船，經馬耳他直取突尼斯灣東端的赫爾梅奧角登陸，距迦太基約二百四十公里。
第二步是登陸點的選擇與軍紀。貝利撒留沒有直撲迦太基：他在旗艦上召開會議，多數軍官主張立刻攻城，理由是迦太基是王國境內唯一設防城市，其餘城市的城牆已被拆毀以防叛亂。貝利撒留以468年的慘敗為戒，又擔心在海上撞上汪達爾主力艦隊，否決了這個方案，改為在登陸點宿營。同夜，卡洛尼馬斯的部分人馬擅自劫掠附近的曼德里亞庫姆商站，軍紀的漏洞第一天就出現。
第三步是登陸後的展開。帝國軍沿海岸公路北進，約翰的三百騎兵前出至大軍前方三英里作先鋒，六百匈人掩護左翼，貝利撒留自領布契拉里騎兵殿後，防的是蓋利默的襲擊，艦隊則沿海岸線隨軍前進。登陸第二天便有士兵偷摘果園水果，貝利撒留嚴懲並全軍告誡，理由寫得很清楚：一旦軍隊把當地居民逼到蓋利默一方，遠征就失去了一切可能。
第四步是阿德底斯姆的包抄與崩潰。蓋利默計畫三路並進：阿馬圖斯率一部擋住正面並接戰，吉巴蒙德領兩千人攻擊左翼，自己帶主力繞到後方全殲羅馬軍。三路卻沒有接上：阿馬圖斯先到，在偵察中被先鋒擊斃；吉巴蒙德的兩千人撞上匈人側翼全軍覆沒，姪子陣亡；蓋利默本人擊潰了羅馬先頭部隊，卻在戰場上看到兄弟的遺體而遲疑，就這一遲疑，貝利撒留集結主力騎兵反擊，把已經潰散的汪達爾軍徹底打散，蓋利默向西逃往努米底亞。當夜約翰與匈人騎兵留在陣地守夜，步兵天亮後由安東尼娜帶上，全軍當日進抵迦太基城下。
第五步是入城與設防。迦太基居民已開城門慶祝，但貝利撒留擔心夜裡有伏擊，選擇在城外紮營，翌晨才列陣於城牆前，確認無敵軍才進城。他住進王宮，坐上蓋利默為他準備的宴席，同時立即修復被戰火損毀的城牆，艦隊則繞過卡本半島駛入突尼斯湖，停泊在離城約七公里半的斯塔格努姆。
第六步是蓋利默的反擊與帝國軍的守城。蓋利默在布拉雷吉亞站穩腳跟，靠散財拉攏當地，靠切斷城外引水渠掐住城內用水，派人進城策反，又向汪達爾人的盟軍——那些被強迫渡海的匈人——散布不滿。最大的叛變風險來自匈人盟軍，貝利撒留以「勝利後重賞並准許回鄉」的承諾穩住他們，同時把一名企圖投敵的迦太基市民釘在木樁上示眾，寧可讓城內震動也不容忍一次成功的策反。戰術上這是典型的以時間換空間：整個冬天都花在修牆、守水、穩定盟軍上。
第七步是特里卡馬魯姆的決戰與追擊。十二月中旬，貝利撒留率軍出城，奔向城外約二十八公里的汪達爾設防營地，與阿德底斯姆時一樣讓騎兵走在步兵之前。這是一場純粹的騎兵戰，而且帝國軍在數量上明顯劣勢：雙方都把最不可靠的部隊——柏柏爾人與匈人——留作預備隊。約翰率隊反覆衝鋒汪達爾中央，陣中殺死察佐；隨後全線發動總攻，汪達爾軍崩潰，棄營而去，蓋利默只帶數名隨從逃入努米底亞。約翰的追兵緊追五天五夜，就在即將追上之時約翰意外陣亡，隊伍停下來舉哀，蓋利默因此得以逃往希波，最後躲進巴巴山上的梅迪烏斯堡壘，由法拉斯率四百人圍困到次年三月，最後在保證安全的條件下投降。
tacticsEn: Belisarius's method can be broken into seven stages. The first is the crossing of the sea and the war without announcement. The fleet put out in the presence of Justinian, Theodora and the patriarch on or about 21 June 533, and went by Perinthus, Abydos, the Dardanelles and Methoni, rounding Zacynthos and crossing the Ionian against a contrary wind, slowed further by fresh water gone bad; after reaching Sicily, Procopius was sent ahead to Syracuse to gather intelligence, and there he learned the decisive fact: the Vandals had no idea the imperial fleet was coming, and Gelimer had gone inland with Tzazo to Sardinia. Belisarius re-embarked at once, passed Malta, and landed at Hermaeum at the eastern end of the Gulf of Tunis, some two hundred and forty kilometres from Carthage. The second stage is the choice of the landing place and the keeping of discipline. Belisarius did not strike straight for Carthage: he called a council aboard his flagship, and most of the officers wanted an immediate assault, on the ground that Carthage was the only walled city left in the kingdom, the walls of every other town having been pulled down to prevent revolts. Belisarius, mindful of the disaster of 468 and worried about meeting the main Vandal fleet at sea, refused the plan and camped where he had landed. The same night a detachment of Calonymus's men plundered the trading station of Mandracium nearby against orders, and the crack in discipline showed itself on the first day. The third stage is the deployment after the landing. The imperial force marched north along the coastal road, John's three hundred cavalry pushing four and a half kilometres ahead of the column as vanguard, the six hundred Huns covering the left flank, Belisarius himself with the bucephalarian horse bringing up the rear in case Gelimer attacked, and the fleet coasting along beside them. On the second day after the landing soldiers were caught stealing fruit from an orchard; Belisarius punished them in public and addressed the whole army, and the reasoning was written down plainly: if the army drove the local people into Gelimer's hands, the expedition lost every possibility it had. The fourth stage is the envelopment and collapse at Ad Decimum. Gelimer planned three moves at once: Ammatas with one body to block the front and engage, Gibamund with two thousand to strike the left flank, and himself with the main force round to the rear to annihilate the Roman army. The three never came together. Ammatas arrived first and was killed by the vanguard while scouting; Gibamund's two thousand ran into the Huns on the flank and were destroyed, and the nephew died with them; Gelimer himself beat the Roman advance guard, then found his brother's body on the field and hesitated, and in that hesitation Belisarius rallied the main cavalry and counter-attacked, breaking the already disordered Vandal army and driving Gelimer west into Numidia. John's cavalry and the Hunnic horse stayed on the field through the night, the infantry came up with the light and were led in by Antonina, and the whole army stood before Carthage that same day. The fifth stage is the entry into the city and the fortifying of it. The people of Carthage had already thrown the gates open in celebration, but Belisarius, fearing an ambush in the dark, camped outside and only next morning drew the army up along the wall, entered when no enemy appeared, took up residence in the royal palace, and sat down to the banquet Gelimer had prepared for him. At the same time he began repairing the walls damaged by the fighting, while the fleet rounded the Cape Bon peninsula into the Lake of Tunis and anchored at Stagnum, about seven and a half kilometres from the city. The sixth stage is Gelimer's counter-stroke and the defence of the city. Gelimer steadied himself at Bulla Regia, buying the loyalty of the countryside with money, choking the city's water by cutting the aqueduct outside the walls, sending agents into the town, and feeding disaffection to the Vandal auxiliaries, the Huns who had been dragged across the sea unwillingly. The gravest risk of defection lay with the Hunnic foederati, and Belisarius held them with a promise of rich rewards and permission to go home once the war was won; at the same time he had a Carthaginian citizen who meant to go over to the Vandals nailed to a stake in public, preferring to shake the city rather than tolerate one successful attempt at a change of sides. Tactically this was the classic trade of time for space: the whole winter went into repairing walls, holding the water and keeping the auxiliaries steady. The seventh stage is the decision of battle at Tricamarum and the pursuit. In mid-December Belisarius marched out of the city towards the Vandal fortified camp some twenty-eight kilometres away, with the cavalry in front of the infantry as at Ad Decimum. It was a purely cavalry engagement, and the imperial army was clearly outnumbered: both sides kept their least reliable troops, the Berbers and the Huns, in reserve. John charged the Vandal centre repeatedly and killed Tzazo there, after which the whole line advanced in a general attack, the Vandal army broke, abandoned its camp and went, and Gelimer escaped into Numidia with a few companions. John's pursuit ran for five days and nights, and just as it seemed about to close on the king, John was killed unexpectedly; the column halted to mourn him, and Gelimer got away to Hippo, and finally took refuge in the fortress of Medeum on the Mountains of the Moon, where Pharas blockaded him with four hundred men until March of the following year, when he surrendered on terms guaranteeing his safety.
data:
可核對的數字分三類，來源可靠程度不同。第一類是普羅科匹厄斯《汪達爾戰爭史》自述與中文維基所引的數字：遠征艦隊五百艘運輸船、約三萬名水手、九十二艘德羅蒙護衛；陸軍步兵一萬（野戰軍與蠻盟軍各半），騎兵五千，貝利撒留的布契拉里近衛騎兵一千五百至二千人，匈人騎射手六百，赫魯利人騎射手四百，約翰的先鋒騎兵三百；出航日為533年6月21日前後，在佩林圖斯等馬五日、阿比多斯等風四日，7月1日抵梅托尼，途中因黴爛麵包引發痢疾，一次病倒五百人。登陸點在突尼斯灣東端的赫爾梅奧角，離迦太基約二百四十公里（合一百六十二羅馬里），登陸後北進十日抵阿德底斯姆，該地在迦太基以南十里；特里卡馬魯姆營地在城西南約二十八公里。汪達爾一方：全族成年男子徵集的部隊，兵力估計二萬至二萬五千，或三萬至四萬，其中大部分為騎兵；派往撒丁島的是一百二十艘精銳戰艦與五千人；阿德底斯姆一戰中吉巴蒙德部兩千人全滅；梅迪烏斯圍城戰中法拉斯四百人攻堅，折損四分之一。時間線：533年6月出航、9月登陸、12月中旬特里卡馬魯姆、534年3月蓋利默投降、同年3月在君士坦丁堡舉行凱旋；貝利撒留535年任執政官。
第二類是現代研究的估計，必須打折扣：汪達爾人總人口估計十萬至二十萬，故上述兵力的可徵比例偏高；帝國軍騎兵數中文維基作五千至七千，另有資料作五千；普羅科匹厄斯的數字帶有修辭成分，不宜逐條照抄。
第三類是系年的分歧，這點必須交代清楚：中文維基把帝國軍抵達阿德底斯姆繫於9月13日、進迦太基繫於9月15日；而按普羅科匹厄斯與伯里《晚期羅馬帝國史》的通行系年，阿德底斯姆之戰與占領迦太基在533年12月初，特里卡馬魯姆在12月中旬，蓋利默到534年3月才投降。寫這場戰爭的時間線，採用後一套更為穩妥。
還有一類數字必須迴避：迦太基陷落後的劫掠造成大量平民死亡，各家記載互相矛盾，且明顯受文體影響；此處不採任何一個數值，只把劫掠本身視為一次軍事事件——軍隊失去控制、城中秩序崩壞，貝利撒留被部下稱為「獨裁者」，這件事一般被認為與535年1月君士坦丁堡的尼卡暴動直接相關。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes of very different reliability. The first class is what Procopius states of himself in the History of the Wars, together with the figures the Chinese encyclopaedia cites: five hundred transports, about thirty thousand sailors, ninety-two dromons in escort; ten thousand foot, drawn half from the field army and half from the foederati, and five thousand horse; the bucephalarian guard of Belisarius at one thousand five hundred to two thousand; six hundred Hun and four hundred Herulian horse archers, and the three hundred cavalry of John's vanguard; the date of sailing on or about 21 June 533, five days waiting at Perinthus for horses, four at Abydos for wind, arrival at Methoni on 1 July, and on the way a single outbreak of dysentery caused by mouldy bread that put five hundred men down at once. The landing place was Hermaeum at the eastern end of the Gulf of Tunis, about two hundred and forty kilometres from Carthage, or a hundred and sixty-two Roman miles, and the march north from there took ten days to reach Ad Decimum, ten miles south of the city; the Vandal fortified camp at Tricamarum lay some twenty-eight kilometres from the town. On the Vandal side the force was levied from the able-bodied men of the whole tribe, estimated at twenty to twenty-five thousand, or thirty to forty thousand, the greater part of it cavalry; what went to Sardinia was one hundred and twenty war galleys and five thousand men; at Ad Decimum the two thousand men under Gibamund were annihilated; and in the siege of Medeum Pharas attacked with four hundred men and lost a quarter of them. The timeline runs: sailing in June 533, landing in September, Tricamarum in mid-December, Gelimer's surrender in March 534, and the triumph in Constantinople in the same month of March, with Belisarius appointed consul for 535. The second class is modern estimate, and must be discounted: the Vandal population is put at between a hundred thousand and two hundred thousand, so the proportion of the population available for levy in the figures above is high; the Chinese encyclopaedia gives the imperial cavalry as five to seven thousand while other sources give five thousand; and Procopius's numbers are rhetorical in places and should not be copied out one by one. The third class is disagreement over the chronology, and it has to be set out. The Chinese encyclopaedia ties the arrival at Ad Decimum to 13 September and the entry into Carthage to the 15th; the standard chronology drawn from Procopius and from Bury's History of the Later Roman Empire places the battle of Ad Decimum and the capture of Carthage in the first days of December 533, the fighting at Tricamarum in mid-December, and Gelimer's surrender in March 534. For a timeline of this war the second of these is the safer to use. One class of figures has to be avoided altogether: the sack that followed the fall of Carthage caused a great many deaths among the townspeople, the accounts contradict one another and are plainly shaped by their genre; no figure is taken here, and the sack is treated simply as a military event, the army losing control and the order of the city collapsing, after which Belisarius was acclaimed by his men as a sole ruler, a thing generally held to be directly connected with the Nika riots in Constantinople in January 535.
cause:
打起來的原因有四層。最表層是王位糾紛：530年蓋利默推翻並囚禁堂兄希爾德里克，查士丁尼要求他交出希爾德里克，或把這位可能被人利用的前王送到君士坦丁堡，蓋利默以「汪達爾人的內政」為由拒絕。查士丁尼要的其實是一個可以開戰的藉口，他並不真打算讓希爾德里克復位。
第二層是宗教：汪達爾人信阿里烏教派，北非的多數居民信迦克墩教派，胡內里克與貢塔蒙德時期的迫害製造了大量難民與教會的怨恨，出征計畫在君士坦丁堡得到的支持主要來自教會。這層原因也讓戰爭帶上「解放者」的政治資本：北非居民自認是羅馬人，被汪達爾人統治將近一百年。
第三層是帝國自身的戰略時機與財政：532年與薩珊波斯在東方邊境恢復和平，東線壓力解除，查士丁尼得以把野戰軍與盟軍調到西邊；但國庫吃緊，財政官員反對新開一場戰事，468年大敗的記憶又讓貴族與將領膽怯，只有卡帕多西亞人約翰敢公開唱反調卻被壓下。另一個關鍵是外交操作：撒丁島總督戈達斯與的黎波里塔尼亞的普登提烏斯先後宣布脫離汪達爾王國並向帝國求援，學者認為查士丁尼事先在背後推動了這兩場叛亂——這是一場把內亂變成入口的策劃。
第四層最深：蓋利默自己的失政。他奪位後迫害政敵、沒收財產、處死貴族，兩個行省的叛亂因此同時爆發；他把精銳與全部戰船派去撒丁島平叛，結果是海上屏障與大部分主力同時離開本土，而他自己又拒絕了查士丁尼的和解條件，斷掉了唯一能拖延遠征的外交出口。加之北非羅馬居民的敵意、希爾德里克派系的存在與柏柏爾部落的游移，蓋利默在本土實際上孤立。戰爭於是有了雙重面孔：對查士丁尼是收復失地與恢復羅馬世界，對汪達爾是王位危機中的一次生存之戰。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause behind this war. The outermost is a dispute over the throne: in 530 Gelimer overthrew and imprisoned his cousin Hilderic, and Justinian demanded that he either give Hilderic up or send this former king, who might be used by someone, to Constantinople; Gelimer refused on the ground that the matter was the internal affair of the Vandals. What Justinian really wanted was a pretext for war; he had no serious intention of restoring Hilderic. The second layer is religion: the Vandals were Arians, while the great majority of North Africans were Nicene Christians, and the persecutions under Huneric and Gunthamund produced a stream of refugees and a body of resentment in the Church, which is where the expedition drew most of its support in Constantinople. This layer also gave the war its political capital as a war of liberation: the people of North Africa regarded themselves as Romans, and had been ruled by Vandals for close to a century. The third layer is the empire's own strategic moment and its finances: with peace restored on the eastern frontier against the Sassanid Persians in 532, the pressure in the East was lifted and Justinian could move the field army and the auxiliaries to the west; but the treasury was strained, the finance officials opposed opening another war, and the memory of the disaster of 468 made the nobles and the officers timid, so that only John the Cappadocian dared to oppose the expedition in public and was overruled. Another key factor was diplomatic manoeuvring: Godas, the governor of Sardinia, and Pudentius in Tripolitania declared themselves independent of the Vandal kingdom and appealed to the empire for help, and scholars hold that Justinian had pushed both revolts from behind, which is a manoeuvre that turns an internal quarrel into an entrance. The deepest layer is Gelimer's own misgovernment. After the seizure of the throne he persecuted his rivals, confiscated their property and put members of the nobility to death, and the two revolts in the outer provinces broke out together as a result. He sent his best troops and all his warships to Sardinia to put down a revolt, and the effect was that the naval screen and the bulk of his army left the homeland at the same time; and he himself refused the terms of reconciliation offered by Justinian, cutting off the one diplomatic means of delaying the expedition. Add to that the hostility of the Roman population of North Africa, the existence of the Hilderic party, and the shifting mood of the Berber tribes, and Gelimer was isolated in his own country. The war therefore wore two faces at once: for Justinian a recovery of lost ground and the restoration of the Roman world, for the Vandals a fight for survival in a crisis of the succession.
impact:
這場戰爭的直接後果是北非重歸帝國。帝國恢復了對迦太基與原汪達爾疆域的統治，設立阿非利加大區，實際控制範圍大致限於汪達爾王國原有的地界；此後一個多世紀裡，北非是帝國最富庶的屬地之一，直到698年迦太基淪於阿拉伯人之手，阿非利加大區才告終，而它的後身正是查士丁尼時代的軍政區劃。
第二個後果是汪達爾族的解體。王國的軍事階層作為獨立的武裝集團被取消：被俘的汪達爾人被解除武裝，貴族被送往君士坦丁堡，五千名俘虜被編進帝國軍的五個團，成為所謂「查士丁尼的汪達爾人」；留在鄉村的普通汪達爾人則被登記為帝國的佃戶，仍住在從前的土地上。這不是一次換國號的改朝換代，而是一個民族作為戰鬥集團的解散。
第三個後果在羅馬世界內部的政治場。534年3月的凱旋是君士坦丁堡建城以來第一次為一次勝利舉行的公開凱旋，也是半個多世紀以來第一次把這樣的榮耀給一位將軍；戰利品裡有汪達爾王室自455年劫掠羅馬所得的珍寶，包括第二聖殿的猶太燈臺與御用器皿，西哥德王國隨後要求歸還西西里的利利貝烏姆港，正是圍著這些財物與戰利品的分配吵開，最終在535年引發哥德戰爭。帝國軍在迦太基的劫掠中失控，軍隊在城門前向貝利撒留高呼帝號，這件事一般被認為直接推動了535年1月君士坦丁堡的尼卡暴動；暴動之後查士丁尼一世與狄奧多拉的下場，成為東羅馬政治史上最著名的轉折。
第四個後果是戰略示範：以一萬步兵、五千騎兵為核心的遠征軍，在幾乎沒有補給的情況下作戰，靠紀律、靠騎射兵與重裝騎兵的搭配，擊垮了以部落徵集、以騎兵為主的汪達爾軍。帝國此後的西征意大利（535至554年），以及對西西里與撒丁的經營，樣式幾乎照搬這次遠征。最後是文化的層面：迦太基重新成為拉丁-希臘語的世界，帝國把行政、稅制與基督教會堂重新架在北非，此後阿非利加的教父傳統所承接的，就是這套重建。
impactEn: The direct consequence of this war was the return of North Africa to the empire. The empire regained its rule over Carthage and the old Vandal territories, established the prefecture of Africa, and in practice controlled very little beyond the bounds the Vandal kingdom had held. For more than a century afterwards North Africa was among the richest provinces of the empire, until the fall of Carthage to the Arabs in 698 brought the prefecture of Africa to an end, its institutional heir being the exarchate established in the time of Justinian. The second consequence was the dissolution of the Vandal people. The military caste of the kingdom was abolished as an independent armed group: the captured Vandals were disarmed, the nobles were sent to Constantinople, and five thousand prisoners were enrolled into five regiments of the imperial army, the so-called Vandals of Justinian, while ordinary Vandals who remained in the countryside were registered as tenants of the empire and stayed on the lands they had held. This was not a change of dynasty with a new name on the throne, but the dispersal of a people as a fighting force. The third consequence played out in the political life of the Roman world. The triumph of March 534 was the first public celebration of a victory held at Constantinople since the city was founded, and the first in more than half a century to give such an honour to a general; among the spoils were the treasures the Vandal royal house had carried off from Rome in 455, including the Jewish lampstand of the Second Temple and the imperial plate, and the Visigothic claim for the return of Lilybaeum in Sicily, and the dispute over the division of the booty, are what led in 535 to the Gothic War. The imperial troops lost control during the sack of Carthage and acclaimed Belisarius as emperor before the gates, a thing generally held to have pushed directly toward the Nika riots in Constantinople in January 535; and what happened to Justinian and Theodora after the riots is the best known turning point in the political history of the Eastern Roman Empire. The fourth consequence is a demonstration of method: an expeditionary army of ten thousand foot and five thousand horse, fighting with almost no supply, broke a Vandal force levied from the tribe and composed mainly of cavalry, by discipline and by the pairing of horse archers with armoured lancers. The empire's western campaigns in Italy from 535 to 554, and its administration of Sicily and Sardinia, followed this expedition almost model for model. Last comes the cultural layer: Carthage became once again a Latin-Greek world, the empire rebuilt the administration, the tax system and the Christian churches of North Africa, and it is upon that rebuilding that the African fathers of the church later built.

戰爭的結果是汪達爾王國的終結。533年12月中旬特里卡馬魯姆一戰，蓋利默的王牌騎兵被摧毀，他本人只帶數名隨從逃入努米底亞；巴巴山上的梅迪烏斯堡壘被法拉斯率四百人圍困，冬季糧盡，法拉斯屢次致函勸降，蓋利默終於在534年3月接受安全保證，率部眾向貝利撒留投降，隨後被押往迦太基，於同年3月的凱旋中被押入君士坦丁堡競技場。
投降的條件決定了往後二十年的樣子。汪達爾人的武裝被解散，貴族被解送到京師，蓋利默被安置在加拉太的一塊大莊園上；只要他放棄阿里烏教派，本可晉身為元老，他沒有放棄，於是以阿里烏教徒的身份留在帝國邊境，據說在禱告中同時為汪達爾人與皇帝祈禱。五千名被俘的汪達爾人被編入五個團，組成「查士丁尼的汪達爾人」；其餘留在原地的汪達爾人成為帝國的佃戶，繳納固定份額的糧稅。
戰利品的分配也成為日後糾紛的源頭。王室的黃金寶座、鑲寶車、數千塔蘭同的白銀、從羅馬掠來的猶太聖殿器物與御用金器，隨凱旋隊伍進入君士坦丁堡；蓋利默披著紫色長袍走進競技場，普羅科匹厄斯寫他不哭不喊，只反覆念著「虛空的虛空，一切都是虛空」。而帝國沒有就此罷手：貝利撒留隨後被派往撒丁島、科西嘉島、塞普特姆與加迪利亞接替汪達爾人的防務，帝國的邊界推到了大西洋岸；西哥德人趁火打劫、佔了北非對岸的塞普特姆，成為542年貝利撒留圍攻休達時的衝突點。
從更長的視角看，這場戰爭是晚期羅馬世界的一次大規模「復國」實驗，結果是：北非奪回，汪達爾人作為軍事力量消失，迦太基變成帝國的屬地；帝國得到的還有寶藏、土地與一段可以拿來自比的凱旋記憶；帝國付出的則是遠征軍的紀律成本、劫掠造成的政治餘震，以及五年之後就要付出的更大戰爭開支——哥德戰爭正是從這批戰利品的歸屬吵起來的。
resultEn: The result of the war was the end of the Vandal kingdom. At Tricamarum in mid-December 533 the royal cavalry of Gelimer was destroyed, and the king himself escaped into Numidia with only a few companions; the fortress of Medeum on the Mountains of the Moon was blockaded by Pharas with four hundred men, ran short of food in the winter, and Pharas wrote again and again urging surrender, until in March 534 Gelimer accepted guarantees for his safety and gave himself up with his followers to Belisarius, was taken to Carthage, and was brought into the Hippodrome of Constantinople in the triumph of that same March. The terms of the surrender determined the shape of the following twenty years. The Vandal armed force was dissolved, the nobles were sent to the capital, and Gelimer was settled on a large estate in Galatia; had he been willing to abandon Arianism he could have been raised to the rank of senator, and he refused, so he remained in the empire as an Arian on its frontier, and it is said that in his prayers he prayed for the Vandals and for the emperor alike. Five thousand captured Vandals were enrolled into five regiments, the Vandals of Justinian, while those who stayed where they were became tenants of the empire paying a fixed share of grain. The division of the spoils became a source of later quarrels. The golden throne, the jewelled carriages, thousands of pounds of silver, the vessels of the Jewish temple carried off from Rome and the imperial plate of gold all went into Constantinople with the triumphal procession; Gelimer walked into the Hippodrome in a purple robe, and Procopius writes that he neither wept nor cried out but only kept repeating that all is vanity and all is vanity. Nor did the empire stop there. Belisarius was sent on to Sardinia, Corsica, Septem and Gades to take over the defence the Vandals had held, and the frontier of the empire was pushed out to the Atlantic; the Visigoths took advantage of the confusion to seize Septem across the strait from North Africa, which became the point of collision when Belisarius besieged Ceuta in 542. From a longer view, this war was one of the great experiments of the late Roman world in recovering what had been lost. The results were these: North Africa recovered, the Vandals ceased to exist as a military force, and Carthage became a province of the empire. The empire gained treasure, land, and a memory of a triumph to measure itself against. What it paid was the cost of discipline in the field, the political aftershock of the sack, and a far larger war bill falling due five years later, since the Gothic War began as an argument over who owned this haul of treasure.
